Definition: a vine stock (properly, one yielding purple grapes, the richest variety)
BiblicalUsage: The choice vine is the best of the vineyard. Jacob blesses Judah with a foal bound to the choice vine, Isaiah's Lord plants His vineyard with the choicest vine and looks for grapes, and Jeremiah hears God say He planted Israel a noble vine, wholly a right seed, and asks how she turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the vine was planted noble and turned strange by Israel's own choice, and the question God asks is still the right one.
